methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native to 'close the technology gap' signals grassroots peer-to-peer knowledge distribution in a non-metro region, potentially building deep fluency outside traditional tech hubs if sustained beyond one-off events.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's formal partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates institutional AI capability in the state capital, creating a metro hub for innovation but raising questions about whether knowledge diffuses beyond Richmond or remains academically siloed.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Commentary explicitly naming AI data centers as drivers of Virginia's 'urban-rural divide' signals infrastructure concentration in NoVA without corresponding capability distribution, reinforcing geographic inequality in AI economic benefits.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI help assistant - MilitaryNews.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard's 'Amelia' IT assistant represents platform-delivered AI for workforce efficiency—shallow adoption that automates tasks without building deep AI literacy among the shipyard's technical workforce.

signals.title: University of Mary Washington Adds Virginia’s First Master’s Degree in AI in Business - Northern Virginia Magazine
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's first AI in Business master's degree at UMW concentrates advanced AI training capacity in the I-95 corridor, creating credentialed expertise in metro-accessible areas while other regions lack equivalent educational pathways to deep AI skills.
